shape.text: Airtable says a personal access token is prefixed with its ID and is otherwise an opaque, variable-length string, and tells integrators not to rely on a particular length or format.
Airtable states that changes to the token format for newly created tokens are not considered breaking changes.
Airtable documents the Authorization: Bearer header for passing a personal access token and says the legacy api_key URL parameter is not supported for it.
Where the ID prefix ends, how long it is, whether it is a non-secret identifier, and the alphabet and length of the remainder are not established.

unresolved.reason: The pages read say only that tokens are prefixed with their ID and are otherwise opaque and variable-length. Third-party pattern lists show one fixed layout, but the provider says changes for new tokens are not breaking, so that layout is not recorded as the provider's format. A provider statement or an archived page naming the layout by issue date would settle it.

issuance.text: A personal access token is created in the developer token panel with chosen scopes and base or workspace access, and is shown to its creator once; Airtable does not store the token itself.

lifecycle.text: A personal access token does not expire on its own; deleting, regenerating or modifying it ends or changes the old value, and a regenerated token's previous value is rejected.

collisions.text: Whether a personal access token can be told apart from an OAuth access token by its text alone is not established.

unresolved.reason: Airtable documents both as bearer tokens and says both are opaque, variable-length strings; no page read states a distinguishing marker. A provider statement of the distinguishing marker would settle it.

openQuestions.text: Whether the layout of tokens created at different dates, or for enterprise service accounts, is the same is not established.

unresolved.reason: The provider reserves the right to change the format for newly created tokens and gives no dated layout history; the changelog entry read dates only the opacity notice. Dated provider documentation or an archived snapshot of the token page would settle it.
